title: Transparent canary credential rotation and audit anchors for RBAC v2
creator: Asha Menon
description: Create a transparent, low-risk credential rotation flow for API/service keys that integrates with RBAC v2 mappings and the new audit logging schema. Deliver a canary shadow-rotation mechanism, an immutable 'audit anchor' ID attached to rotation events for cross-system tracing (Console, audit logs, SLO dashboards), and a clear operator UX for staged deprecation. Goals: (1) zero-downtime key replacement for in-use service keys where possible, (2) cryptographic/metadata audit anchors to link rotated keys to SAML/SSO session context and RBAC role mappings, (3) automation to detect stale/permanent keys and schedule rotation or expiration, (4) strong observability (traces, counters, failed-switch metrics) to validate rollout safety.
acceptance_criteria: Shadow rotation (create new key + attach to same roles) succeeds for 95% of sampled services without manual reconfiguration
Every rotation emits an audit_anchor (UUID) present in: audit-log event, console timeline entry, related GitHub PR (when rotation initiated via CI), and rotation runbook entry
RBAC v2 mapping service can look up both previous and current key identities and show role continuity in Console
Expired/stale-key detector flags keys older than policy TTL with confidence score and auto-creates rotation tasks
Security review signoff and integration tests validate SSO session continuity for token exchange flows using SAML assertions
non_goals: Not implementing full org-wide forced revoke policy in this ticket
Not changing naming conventions for user-managed keys created outside Redwood (will propose separately)
rollout_plan: MVP: implement shadow-rotation API + audit_anchor metadata (backend + Console flags) in staging
Canary: enable for 10 low-risk internal services, monitor error budget and failed-switch metrics for 48h
Wider rollout: opt-in for Dedicated customers and platform-managed service keys
Enforcement: after 6 weeks, automate stale-key tasks and soft warnings in Console; evaluate hard expiration policy

engineering_notes: Decision: use shadow-rotation (create-and-attach) instead of immediate swap to reduce blast radius and allow traffic rollout via feature flags
Trade-off: shadow increases short-term key volume and requires audit log correlation; mitigated by audit_anchor and short retention for intermediate keys

Implementation detail: audit_anchor is stored as top-level metadata on rotation event and included in structured audit log (jsonPayload.audit_anchor). Console will surface anchor in timeline entries for traceability
Observability: add rotation-runbook-dashboard with counters: rotation_attempts, rotation_successes, rotation_rollbacks, failed_switch_rate, stale_key_count
RBAC mapping: extend v2 role-mapper to accept key_alias and audit_anchor when reconciling roles after rotation
SSO/SAML: include SAML assertion id (when available) in audit_anchor metadata; when absent, fallback to operator principal id
